acceptance_criteria: AC-1 A single new migration, V21, adds the role column with a CHECK constraint over exactly the two named values.
AC-2 Every pre-existing device row is backfilled to the gateway value and the column is not nullable afterwards.
AC-3 A device added through the existing path carries an explicit role, and a round trip through the repository returns it unchanged.
AC-4 A value outside the vocabulary is refused by the database, and a test proves it.
AC-5 The service starts against the migrated schema; if the migration writes to an audited table it sets the actor fingerprint and action id transaction-locally.
AC-6 The ui2 persistence and service test suites pass, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14I_ARTEFACT_LOCATION_OPERATOR_RETRIEVAL_DEVIATION_AND_MANAGEMENT_SERVERS.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner directives 2026-09-14. MS-1: a management server or MDS, and a Panorama, are devices in their own right, added through the same one add menu, holding the same device row, carrying the same enrollment and confirm path. MS-2: inventory, configuration and backup are collected from them with their own per-vendor read sets, and nothing is issued against one until its own gate entries exist. MS-3: this does not reopen collection through the management server. MS-5: until MS-2's gates exist, a management server is a device that can be discovered from and confirmed, and whose collection actions are refused with a reason naming the missing gate.
baseline.engineering_baseline: ui2/persistence owns the device row and its repository; migrations live in ui2/service/src/main/resources/db/migration and the highest version present is V20.
baseline.product_baseline: Devices are added, enrolled and confirmed today; discovery reads from a management plane but the manager itself is not a device row. Collection is gated per capability. Nothing in this movement issues a command to any device.
baseline.test_baseline: The ui2 persistence and service test suites pass on origin/main today.

so the column set is declared in more than one place and every one of them has to agree. vendor_hint already carries the vendor (check_point, palo_alto); this movement adds what the device IS, which is a different axis from who made it.

invariants: Identifiers and vocabularies are opaque and closed: the role is one of exactly the two named values, enforced by the database and not only by Java.
No command, route or read set reaches a management server in this movement.
One migration, one version, no edit to an existing migration file.
A migration writing to an audited table sets its actor fingerprint and action id transaction-locally.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Let a device say what kind of device it is. Record 14I MS-1 makes a Check Point management server or MDS, and a Panorama, devices in their own right rather than merely discovery sources -- but nothing in the model distinguishes one from a gateway, so MS-5's refusal cannot even be expressed. This movement adds that distinction to the device model and nothing else; the refusal, the read sets and their command gates are separate movements that depend on it.
output_contract: A device row that can say whether it is a gateway or the management server that governs one.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One migration and one field carried through a named set of places; no vendor semantics and no device interaction.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
The gradle commands run from ui2; the privacy gate runs from the repository root.
Every changed file names the clause it implements (14I MS-n).
Run only the commands named above.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE names the two role values you chose, every place the column set is declared, and whether the migration touched an audited table.
risks: Taking a migration version another movement is already using. V21 is assigned to this movement and to nothing else; do not pick the next free number yourself.
Missing one of the places the column set is named -- there is more than one constant plus an insert plus a mapper, and a miss shows only at runtime.
Making the column nullable to avoid the backfill, which leaves the model unable to answer the question it exists to answer.
Writing to an audited table without the transaction-local settings, which crash-loops the service at rollout rather than failing in a test.

in: One migration, numbered V21 and no other number, adding a device-role column to the devices table with a CHECK constraint over a closed vocabulary. The vocabulary is exactly two values in this movement: a gateway or enforcement device, and a management server. Name them plainly and write the names into the constraint.
Every existing row is backfilled to the gateway value, because every device enrolled so far is one. The column is not nullable after the backfill.

If the migration writes to a table whose changes are audited, it must set app.actor_fingerprint and app.action_id transaction-locally, or the service crash-loops on start. A test in this repository enforces it; read an existing migration that writes to an audited table and follow it exactly.
DeviceRecord and JooqDeviceRepository carry the new field through: the record component, both column constants, the insert, and the row mapper. Every place that names the column set must agree.
The add-device path sets the role explicitly rather than defaulting silently, so a device added from now on states what it is.
Tests: the migration applies and backfills; a round trip through the repository preserves the role; an unknown value is refused by the constraint.
out: Any refusal behaviour. MS-5's refusal, its reason text and the gate it names are a separate movement that depends on this one.
Any read set, any command, any API route to a management server. MS-2 forbids issuing anything until its own gate entries exist, and none exist.
Any change to vendor_hint or to the enrollment states. The role is a different axis from the vendor and from the enrollment lifecycle.
Any UI change. The device workspace is not touched by this movement.
Any migration version other than V21, and any edit to an existing migration file.

completed: Added migration V21__device_role.sql adding role column to devices table with CHECK constraint (role IN ('gateway', 'management_server')), backfilling existing rows to 'gateway' and setting NOT NULL.
The migration touched the audited table devices and transaction-locally set app.actor_fingerprint and app.action_id via set_config to prevent audit logging crash-loops.
The two role values chosen are 'gateway' and 'management_server'.
Carried the role field through DeviceRecord, DeviceSummaryRecord, DeviceDraft, and JooqDeviceRepository.
Every place the column set is declared (DEVICE_COLUMNS, DEVICE_SUMMARY_COLUMNS, INSERT query, and row mappers) now agrees.

The add-device path (DeviceRegistrationService, DeviceAddSingleService, DeviceRegistrationController) sets the role explicitly rather than defaulting silently, and discovery import specifies role 'gateway'.
Added invalidRoleIsRefused test in DeviceRegistrationServiceTest, verified all persistence and service tests pass, and verified repository privacy check.
